app.notConnected: No device is connected. Connect one from the Device tab first.

selection.none: Nothing selected — changes apply to every key

notDecoded.title: {what} — protocol not decoded
notDecoded.body: This panel turns itself on as soon as a codec implements the command. Find the command with Explorer → Console → Prober first, then add a codec under src/protocol/.

apply.noWrite: The active codec ({codec}) does not support writing.

unknown.label: Not decoded (raw mode)
unknown.notes: The protocol has not been decoded yet. Explorer, console, prober and the traffic log all still work.

raven61.label: Raven61 (reads decoded)
raven61.notes: Packet framing, analog key events, the per-key performance read (0xa0) and the global settings read (0x05) are decoded. The write (0xa1) is decoded down to the encoder but has not been verified against hardware, so it is not wired up yet.

raven61.slotMapPartial: Only {found}/{total} keys were resolved from the keymap; falling back to the guessed slot mapping.
raven61.slotMapFailed: Keymap read failed; falling back to the guessed slot mapping: {reason}
raven61.emptySlots: {count} key slots are empty in the performance block: {keys}

device.title: Device

unsupported.title: This browser does not support WebHID.
unsupported.body: Open it in desktop Chrome, Edge or Opera. The page must be served over HTTPS or from localhost.

raven.label: Raven family (VID 0x19F5)
raven.hint: The device ids the stock driver recognises. This is usually the one you want.

all.label: All HID devices
all.hint: For when nothing shows up above. Lists every HID device Chrome can reach.

vendorPages.label: Vendor-defined pages
vendorPages.hint: Only the usage pages commonly used as a configuration channel.

device.wrongInterface: The interface currently open does not look like the configuration channel. Open the one marked recommended in the list below, or no key travel will reach the monitor.
device.knownHint: Interfaces you have already granted access to. One keyboard showing up as several is normal, and only one of them carries configuration and the monitor stream — the recommended one with the highest score.

actuation.title: Actuation point
actuation.counts: mm = {counts} counts (in steps of {step} mm) · out of {travel} mm total travel

rt.title: Rapid trigger
rt.enable: Enable rapid trigger on the selected keys
rt.continuous: Continuous mode (works above the actuation point too)
rt.noise: The board's smallest step is {step} mm, and the factory default is 0.10 mm for both press and release. Going below that can let sensor noise through as real input, so check the resting jitter on the Monitor tab first.

deadzone.title: Dead zone
deadzone.hint: The stretch at each end of the stroke that is ignored. Same as the stock driver's Top / Bottom dead zone.
deadzone.enable: Enable dead zone on the selected keys

advanced.title: Advanced keys (DKS · MT · TGL · RS · SOCD · OKS)
advanced.note: The stock driver stores up to 40 advanced keys per profile and tells the kinds apart by <c>t_magnetic_key_data.macro_type</c>. DKS keeps its four depth-stage actions in <c>t_key_item_data.trigger_state1..4</c>.

calibration.title: Bottom-out calibration
calibration.how: Calibration has no command of its own — holding the analog test mode open is the calibration. {command} is resent every {rearmMs} ms to keep the mode open, and every key pressed all the way down while it is held relearns its bottom-out magnet value (the same thing the stock driver's performance tab does).
calibration.warning: ⚠ You cannot type on this keyboard while it runs. Typing comes back the moment you stop. Recalibrating also moves the bottom that actuation and rapid trigger are measured from — only run it when you need it.
calibration.progressHint: counts keys seen at {mm} mm or deeper
calibration.fillHint: The fill is the deepest travel seen this pass — an empty key is one you have not pressed yet.

perf.title: Current board settings
perf.needDevice: Once a device is connected, all {keys} keys are read back from the board. Connect one from the Device tab first.
perf.bottomOutNote: This one is a global setting rather than a per-key one (0x05 block, payload[15] bit 1).
perf.sameByte: Same byte: Tachyon {tachyon} · actuation_check {actuationCheck} · magnet test {magnetTest} · debounce {debounce}
perf.uniform: Every key has the same settings

emptySlots.note: An all-zero record decodes as actuation {mm} mm · RT off · {switchName}. That is not a real setting — it is a failed read.

perf.footnote: Values are in mm and the board's smallest step is {step} mm. The table shows what was read from the board as-is; edits made in the panels below do nothing until you apply to board.

keymap.title: Keymap
keymap.transparent: ▽ = transparent (falls through to the layer below).
keymap.pickHint: Pick a key, then assign a code below.
keymap.writeNote: The keymap command is usually long enough to be split across several reports. Change one key in the stock driver, save, and diff the captures: the byte that moved is that key's index — the most reliable way to work out the matrix order.

language.title: Language
language.hint: Your choice is stored in this browser only.

debug.label: Debug mode
debug.hint: Shows the Debug tab — the live monitor at the top, then the analysis panels (observed identities · key address candidates · baseline ADC drift) and the tools (explorer · console · prober · events · log). They exist for decoding the protocol, so you do not normally need them.

keyId.title: Key identification
keyId.label: Ignore the built-in table — use my own bindings only
keyId.hint: All 61 keys now name themselves in the event stream (modifiers through the HID modifier bitmask in payload[2]), so this table is only a fallback. It guesses a key from its sensor value and baseline ADC, both of which calibration changes — and a stale table guesses wrong rather than not at all. Turn it off when that happens.

storage.title: What gets stored
storage.hint: The settings above and the sensor addresses you bind on the Events tab live in this browser's localStorage only. Nothing is written to the board, so opening this on another PC starts from the defaults.

explorer.label: Explorer
explorer.hint: Report descriptor tree, with the usable report ids and their lengths

console.label: Console
console.hint: Send commands as frames or blocks; repeat one and see which bytes move

prober.label: Prober
prober.hint: Sweep commands as real frames (checksum handled) and see what answers

events.label: Events
events.hint: Listen to what the board sends unasked, and bind sensor addresses

log.label: Log
log.hint: Every report in and out, A/B byte diff, TXT and JSON export

explorer.title: HID explorer
explorer.hint: The report descriptor as the browser parsed it. Check the report ids you can send, and their exact lengths, here.
explorer.chromeNote: Chrome deliberately does not expose the keyboard top-level collections (0x01/0x06) to WebHID. Their absence here is not a fault — configuration goes through the vendor-defined collection.

console.title: Report console
console.payloadPlaceholder: e.g. 55 a9 00 00   (you supply the checksum yourself)
console.badCommand: The command must be in the range 00–ff

reply.ack: ACK — command {command} was received, no data

console.constant: Every byte was identical across {count} repeats — these are constants, not live values.
console.moving: Bytes that moved: {offsets} — those are the live ones.

prober.title: Command prober

warning.title: Careful — this sends commands nobody has identified yet.
warning.body: 0x01 (begin) and 0x02 (end/commit) appear to open and close a settings transaction. What the commands in between write is still unknown, so a settings reset or a flash write is possible. The stock driver warns that this board needs key calibration after a firmware upgrade — meaning a command that touches calibration exists too. Back your settings up with the stock driver first.

prober.knownOnly: Only try the {count} commands the stock driver actually sends (recommended)
prober.safeOnly: Send only the commands confirmed safe ({commands}). The rest are block writes, and sending one with an empty payload can zero the start of a firmware blob.
prober.wrap: Wrap each command in a 0x01 … 0x02 transaction (the stock driver's own order)
prober.acknowledge: I understand the risk and have backed my settings up
prober.noAnswer: Nothing answered. If the stock driver is running it may hold the device exclusively — close it and try again. If that changes nothing, try a different report id or mode.
prober.legend: ★ = a command the stock driver actually sends (0x01 begin, 0x02 end/commit, {globalSettings} global settings) · ⚠ = a command observed to change board state when sent with an empty payload
prober.badRange: That sweep range is not valid (00–ff).

events.title: Event listener
events.intro: Listens to the reports the board sends without being asked. The stock driver polls these in a loop of its own and treats every report starting with 0xa0 as an event. Listening alone sends nothing. The board only streams once it has been armed though (spec §3.2), so if nothing arrives, turn on arm stream below as well. Reporting is enabled and the test mode exited right after, so typing keeps working and nothing is recalibrated.
events.armStream: Arm stream ({arm} → {disarm}) — typing is disabled while arming
events.silent: Nothing has arrived yet. Try pressing a key, and if that changes nothing turn on arm stream — the board sends nothing at all until it is armed.
events.pressHint: Press the keys one at a time. Any key left grey has no sensor address bound to it yet.
events.bindHint: Pick the key to bind from the grid ({fingerprint}).
events.unbound_one: {count} key does not name itself. Modifiers and Fn are reported as a HID bitmask and so carry no usage (0x00, or 0x01 for Fn). Pick one below, then click the matching key in the grid above to bind it. The identity is the sensor value plus the baseline ADC — the sensor value alone collides for some keys.
events.unbound_other: {count} keys do not name themselves. Modifiers and Fn are reported as a HID bitmask and so carry no usage (0x00, or 0x01 for Fn). Pick one below, then click the matching key in the grid above to bind it. The identity is the sensor value plus the baseline ADC — the sensor value alone collides for some keys.
events.notAnalog: Not in the analog key event format
events.noMoving: All {count} were identical — no byte moved.

log.title: Traffic log
log.hint_one: Click a line to mark it A/B and see the byte differences between the two reports. {count} entry.
log.hint_other: Click a line to mark it A/B and see the byte differences between the two reports. {count} entries.

sensors.title: Live key travel · ADC
sensors.intro: Shows exactly what the board sends — live key travel and every raw sensor number behind it (current ADC, the resting baseline ADC, sensor delta, sensor value). The board does not report a key it is not being pressed, so the grid only fills in as you press each key once.
sensors.focus: Focus #{index} {key} — click a key to change it
sensors.uncalibrated: Some keys are not calibrated. They report a total stroke of 0, so the travel shown is an estimate scaled against the nominal {nominal} mm. One calibration pass replaces it with the measured value.
sensors.staleTable: The built-in identity table does not match this board. Either a sensor value missing from the table showed up on an unnamed key, or more baselines were seen under one sensor value than that value has keys. As it stands, a modifier can resolve to the wrong key — turn on Ignore the built-in table under Settings and bind them yourself on the Events tab.
sensors.armFailedHint: Check that the interface marked recommended on the Device tab is the one that is open.
sensors.armed: Analog reporting is on (<c>{arm}</c> → <c>{disarm}</c>). Reporting stays enabled while the test mode has been exited, so typing keeps working and nothing is recalibrated.
sensors.gridLegend: The fill is the current travel; the number below it is travel mm / current ADC.
sensors.drifted: The baseline ADC has drifted. A baseline is a stored calibration constant, so a value changing within one session — or more values under one sensor value than it has keys — means a recalibration happened in between. The drift panel below shows how far it is from the built-in table.
sensors.unresolvedHint_one: {count} unresolved identity can be bound to a key on the Events tab.
sensors.unresolvedHint_other: {count} unresolved identities can be bound to keys on the Events tab.
sensors.notAKeyHint: {count} not-a-key reports — no usage, no modifier bits and no baseline ADC ({ids}). A healthy board keeps sending these, so they are left out of key identification.

address.title: Key address candidates — finding a byte that does not drift
address.intro: Taking the {groups} keys that name themselves through a usage as ground truth, every byte is checked two ways: is it always the same value within one key, and does it differ between keys? A byte that does both is a key address that calibration cannot shake.
address.found: An undecoded byte meets the address criteria. If it also differs across the modifiers, keys can be identified by this byte instead of by their fingerprint — regardless of calibration.
address.none: No undecoded byte meets the address criteria. That may just be too few samples, so press each key several times at different depths. If none turns up, this event carries no calibration-safe identifier and modifiers have to rely on your own bindings.
address.unnamedCheck: Whether the candidate bytes really do differ across the unnamed keys (modifiers · Fn):

drift.title: Baseline ADC drift — against the built-in table
drift.intro: For each entry in <c>fingerprints.ts</c>, the closest baseline ADC observed under the same sensor value. The tolerance is ±{tolerance}; beyond that the key either fails to resolve or resolves to a different key.

note.ambiguous: indistinguishable from another key on the same sensor value
note.outOfRange: outside tolerance — this key will not resolve

drift.copySource: Copy the updated table as source
drift.copyHint: Rewrites <c>KEY_FINGERPRINTS</c> with the observed baseline ADCs — key assignments stay as they are, only the numbers change.
drift.ambiguous: Some pairs are ambiguous. Two keys under the same sensor value have observations close enough that this table alone cannot say which observation belongs to which key. Bind those keys yourself on the Events tab by pressing them one at a time — your own bindings win over the built-in table.

trace.title: Trace — #{index} {key}
trace.noise: resting jitter {mm} mm — rapid trigger sensitivity must be larger than this
